transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~36 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Kris O'Connell (Redwood CSM); Samir Patel (CTO, LumenAI), Emily Wong (ML Engineer), Maya Ortiz (Infra), Carlos (Product)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): LumenAI is exploring Redwood for inference for their chat and summarization features. Primary asks: quick time-to-first-token for devs, free credits for experimentation, clear path to dedicated capacity if needed, and security assurances. They have tight latency SLO (~150-200ms for short chat flows) and care about token costs.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, i'm jordan from redwood, and i'll run through a quick agenda: understand your current stack, what you're trying to ship, and how you evaluate hosted vs dedicated/private. priya from our se team is here for the deep bits.
[00:12] Samir: cool thanks, uh yeah i'm samir cto at lumenAI, on the call are emily and maya, carlos as product — we're curious about quickstarts, like how fast our engineers can get from sign-up to first token, and what limits are in the free trial.
[00:25] Priya: great question. with our PLG quickstart we usually see engineers making first requests in under 30 minutes if they follow the cURL/SDK steps; free credits are applied at signup, and there's a clear path to convert to reserved capacity if throughput or data residency become blockers.
[00:40] Emily: 30 mins? that's optimistic but sounds good. what's in the quickstart — is there a sample repo or a hosted playground?
[00:48] Jordan: yes we provide a quickstart repo, a hosted sandbox, and sample prompts. i'll share links after the call. free credits cover initial usage — enough to run basic evals and a small benchmark.
[01:05] Maya: on the infra side i'm worried about data residency and VPCs. we have some regulated customers and will need private deployment options. can you run in our vpc?
[01:15] Priya: we support three modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private (VPC/on-prem). for VPC we have a private control plane option and integrations with customer KMS. in those cases onboarding takes longer, usually weeks not hours, because of network setup and compliance reviews.
[01:33] Samir: timeline question — we are two teams: product wants to play with hosted first via quickstart, then if performance and security check out we might move to dedicated. is that a typical path?
[01:43] Jordan: absolutely. many customers start PLG/self-serve -> proof-of-value -> reserved/dedicated. the important bit is we can route dev traffic to hosted while you prep dedicated.
[01:53] Carlos: are there any caps on streaming or token rates during the free trial? we have spikes from demos.
[01:59] Jordan: trials have soft rate limits that we can relax for pilot benchmarks — just ask. for production you pick a plan or reserved capacity.
[02:12] Priya: quick bit on latency: what are your SLOs and typical request sizes? that guides batching and model choice.
[02:20] Emily: target is 150ms p95 for short chat turns (under 200 tokens typical), but for async summarization we can tolerate higher latencies. cost is also a big driver; we want to compare per-token costs and also how caching/prefix caching might save dollars.
[02:36] Priya: makes sense. for p95 150ms you'll likely want optimized model variants on GPU and small seq lengths; we can recommend quantization and batching settings. caching helps for repeated prompts, but chat KV caching is tricky if you have dynamic user context.
[02:52] Samir: security — do you have SOC2? what about SSO and audit logs?
[02:58] Jordan: yes SOC2 Type II, SAML/SSO for enterprise accounts, role-based access, and audit logs available in the console. for private deployments we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for key management. i'll attach our security pack.
[03:15] Maya: how about data retention and deletion? we need to ensure customer data isn't used to train models.
[03:20] Priya: for hosted we have options to opt out of data retention and we also have an enterprise contract addendum for data non-training. dedicated or private means data stays in your environment per the deployment model.
[03:33] Carlos: pricing — do you publish per-token rates and discounts for reserved capacity?
[03:37] Jordan: yes we have usage-based pricing for hosted, and reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated with better unit economics. i'll send the pricing grid; for pilots we often give promo credits to help measure ROI.
[03:48] Emily: ok on benchmarking — we want to run a small throughput/latency test comparing a couple Open models. do you support running our benchmark harness against hosted endpoints?
[03:57] Priya: yes, we can whitelist IPs or relax trial limits for the benchmark; we'll share a benchmark template. also note streaming vs non-streaming affects apparent latency.
[04:12] Samir: any gotchas on model compatibility? we use a custom tokenizer in one flow; can we bring our own model?
[04:20] Priya: we support a model catalog with open models; for BYOM (bring your own model) that's more common on Dedicated/Private where you can load custom artifacts. hosted is curated models. if you need custom tokenizer support we can discuss Dedicated/Private options.
[04:36] Jordan: quick practical: to get started i'll send: 1) quickstart repo link and cURL examples, 2) pricing and free credits details, 3) security pack, 4) benchmark template. can we target sending those today or tomorrow?
[04:50] Samir: tomorrow works. we'd like to loop in procurement early — any typical procurement docs?
[04:56] Jordan: we'll include a procurement checklist and sample contract terms.
[05:05] Maya: one more infra detail — we run in AWS across us-east-1 and eu-west-1, we'd want region affinity for latency and data residency. you have regions?
[05:15] Priya: yes hosted has multi-regions and we can pin routing by region; Dedicated can be provisioned in specific clouds/regions. we'll note your regions in the pilot plan.
[05:28] Emily: what about SDK language support? we use python and node.
[05:32] Jordan: SDKs for python, node, and go; cURL also. sample code in the quickstart repo.
[05:40] Carlos: any mention of cost-optimizations like quantization guidance?
[05:44] Priya: yes we have Optimize recommendations — quantization, batching, and kernel selection based on model and seq length. for short real-time chat you might prefer a faster fp16 variant; for batch summarization quantized variants save cost.
[06:01] Samir: okay sounds good. can we do a short pilot: hosted quickstart with free credits, run our benchmark, then re-eval for dedicated?
[06:08] Jordan: yes that's the typical flow. proposed next steps: i'll send artifacts, priya will share benchmark template, then we schedule a pilot kickoff next week.
[06:18] Emily: would love a dev sandbox for the team so they can iterate without affecting prod keys.
[06:23] Jordan: we can create sandbox API keys and a sample workspace.
[06:29] Samir: any red flags we should be aware of? like if we hit rate limits or p95 spikes — what's the support SLA?
[06:36] Kris: as CSM i'll be your point for pilot support; we have SLAs for Dedicated, and for hosted pilots we provide dev support and can escalate to SEs if benchmarks need tuning.
[06:48] Maya: make sure the security pack answers our questions on KMS and audit logs or we'll need a deeper security call.
[06:55] Jordan: noted, i'll include the security deck.
[07:00] Carlos: ok minor nit — when you say 30 minutes to first token, does that include account verification steps? sometimes corporate SSO slows things down.
[07:08] Jordan: fair point — 30 mins is for devs who can sign up freely; with enterprise SSO it can be longer. for quickstarts we recommend devs use personal signups and then migrate.
[07:21] Emily: for the benchmark i'll send a small prompt set and traffic profile — mostly short chats (~50-150 tokens), some 800-1k summarization jobs.
[07:30] Samir: timeline — procurement and security review might take 2-4 weeks, but engineering wants to start early.
[07:36] Jordan: that's expected. we'll provide docs to speed procurement.
[07:42] Priya: a quick technical note — for p95 latency below 200ms on GPU, it's often about optimizing sequence length and avoiding large context windows; we can recommend model variants during the pilot.
[07:56] Maya: are there examples of customers who started PLG and moved to dedicated? any case study?
[08:02] Jordan: yes we'll share a short case study; many scale that way.
[08:10] Emily: ok let's recap next steps.
[08:13] Jordan: recap: 1) Send quickstart repo, cURL samples, SDK links; 2) Send pricing + free credits info; 3) Send security pack; 4) Priya to share benchmark template and sample prompts; 5) Create sandbox API keys; 6) schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2026-11-24.
[08:35] Samir: agreed. thanks everyone, look forward to the materials.
[08:40] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up shortly.

End of transcript.
